main_issue: How to deal with the unwashed pork-fat pan tonight so D (who needs a clay ritual wash) can cook, and whether to adopt a wash-after-use rule going forward

A-B.evidence: A suggests D order in (T11) and B later offers to pay for D's food (T14) — both aim at D eating without using the pan; both accept the pan is not usable tonight, though neither speaks directly to the other's proposal.

A-C.evidence: C proposes wash-after-use rule (T3, T15) and soap wash (T9); A asks about clay (T7) and says D can't use the pan (T13), no direct agreement or rejection of the rule.

A-D.evidence: A asks about the wash (T5, T7), accepts D can't use the pan and suggests ordering in (T11); D rejects it as unaffordable (T12) and insists on cooking, and A repeats the pan is unusable (T13).

B-C.evidence: C accepts B's payment offer as 'good for tonight' (T15) and keeps pushing the rule; B just wants to end it (T14).

B-D.evidence: B dismisses clay as unrealistic (T8) and offers to pay (T14); D declines, 'I'd feel bad taking your money' (T16), and still asks what to do about the pan.

C-D.evidence: D calls C's wash-after-use rule 'a good rule' (T4, T16) but rejects C's soap-wash idea (T10) and insists on solving tonight's pan.
